newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-EASTERN CONFERENCE STARS WINS SUPERSKILLS COMPETITION.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-EASTERN CONFERENCE STARS WINS SUPERSKILLS COMPETITION.

text.p: The Eastern Conference posted a 13-7 win over the West Friday in the NHL SuperSkills competition at the All-Star Game celebration.
The competition featured six events -- puck control relay, rapid fire shooting, hardest shot, fastest skater, accuracy shooting and breakaway relay.
On the individual level, Peter Bondra of the Washington Capitals was the fastest skater with a time of 13.61 seconds, edging Geoff Sanderson of the Hartford Whalers.

Al MacInnis of the St. Louis Blues again had the hardest shot at 98.9 miles per hour (160 kph), slightly ahead of Sanderson. It was the third hardest-shot victory for MacInnis, who also won in 1991 and 1992.

Ray Bourque of the Boston Bruins, who will play in his 15th All-Star Game Saturday, captured his fourth title as most accurate shot, shattering four targets on only seven shots. Owen Nolan of the San Jose Sharks and Brendan Shanahan of the Detroit Red Wings also hit four targets, but both needed the maximum eight shots.

John Vanbiesbrouck of the Florida Panthers was the top goaltender for the second time. He stopped all 10 attempts in the rapid-fire relay, then made saves on 4-of-6 efforts in the breakaway relay. Vanbiesbrouck shared top goalie honours with Patrick Roy at the 1994 All-Star Game.
The All-Star Game will be played on Saturday.
